title: DEV_BYPASS must never activate outside NODE_ENV=development, even when DEV_BYPASS=true is set
description: authenticate.js gates the dev bypass with `const DEV_BYPASS = process.env.DEV_BYPASS === 'true' && process.env.NODE_ENV === 'development'` (allow-list, not deny-list, specifically because the Docker image bakes NODE_ENV=development as its default). If NODE_ENV is anything other than 'development' the hardcoded org (DEV_ORG_ID, default 6897584a54a19172fda820b6) and user must never be assigned to req.orgId/req.userId. Regression guard for a prior finding (TI-001 in QA_Tracker/TENANT_ISOLATION) that characterized this as an unconditional bypass.
preconditions: Build/deploy vibrantix-backend with DEV_BYPASS=true and NODE_ENV=production (or staging/test)
No Authorization header available
steps: Start the backend with env NODE_ENV=production, DEV_BYPASS=true
Call any authenticated route (e.g. GET /api/risks) without a Bearer token
Repeat with NODE_ENV=staging and NODE_ENV=test
expectedResult: In every non-development NODE_ENV, the request is rejected with 401 'No token provided' — req.orgId is never set to the hardcoded DEV_ORG_ID and no data is returned. Only NODE_ENV=development with DEV_BYPASS=true assigns the dev org/user.

title: Internal service-token endpoint rejects requests presenting a valid x-organization-id header but no (or an invalid) x-service-token
description: authenticate.js grants SUPERADMIN-equivalent access (req.userRoles=[{systemRoleKey:'SUPERADMIN'}], req.permissions={'project.admin'}) to any request whose x-service-token header exactly matches INTERNAL_SERVICE_TOKEN, and trusts the caller-supplied x-organization-id header verbatim as req.orgId with no further validation against a real ClientOrganization record. This is by design for legitimate internal callers (e.g. audit-report-generator Celery workers), but the entire tenant-scoping guarantee for this path rests on INTERNAL_SERVICE_TOKEN never leaking. This case verifies the token check itself cannot be bypassed by header presence alone.
preconditions: INTERNAL_SERVICE_TOKEN configured on the backend
Attacker does not know the real token value
steps: Call an internal-only endpoint with header x-service-token: wrong-or-missing and x-organization-id: <victim-org-id>
Call the same endpoint with x-service-token: <correct token> and x-organization-id: <arbitrary-org-id>
Inspect req.orgId resolution and the response for both cases
expectedResult: Step 1 is rejected as a normal (non-service) request — falls through to standard JWT auth and returns 401 without a Bearer token, never reaching the SUPERADMIN-equivalent code path. Step 2 succeeds and req.orgId is set to whatever org id was supplied — confirming that org-scoping on this path is enforced ENTIRELY by secrecy of INTERNAL_SERVICE_TOKEN, which must be flagged for periodic rotation and restricted network exposure (internal service mesh only, never internet-reachable).

title: vendor-service refuses to start with BYPASS_PERMISSIONS=true when NODE_ENV=production
description: vendor-service/src/plugins/keycloak.ts:223-225 throws `new Error('BYPASS_PERMISSIONS must not be true in production')` at startup when both NODE_ENV==='production' and BYPASS_PERMISSIONS==='true'. This is a regression guard verifying that hard-stop still fires and cannot be silently skipped.
preconditions: vendor-service deployable with configurable env vars
steps: Start vendor-service with NODE_ENV=production and BYPASS_PERMISSIONS=true
Observe process startup outcome
expectedResult: The service throws at startup and refuses to accept traffic — process exits non-zero rather than starting with all permission/role checks (requirePermission, requireRole) disabled.

title: Vendor detail endpoint (clientVendorService.getById) rejects a vendor ID belonging to another organization
description: vendor-service/src/routes/client-vendor.routes.ts resolves orgId from the authenticated caller (orgStr(req)) and passes it as the first argument to clientVendorService.getById(orgId, req.params.id, userId). This verifies the service-layer lookup actually scopes by orgId (not just permission role) — the classic tenant IDOR check independent of the BYPASS_PERMISSIONS role gate covered in TISO-SEC-003.
preconditions: Two orgs (A, B), each with at least one vendor record
Valid JWT for a user in org A with vendor.read permission
steps: As an org A user, call GET /vendors/:id (client-vendor route) using a vendor ID that belongs to org B
expectedResult: Request returns 403/404 — no vendor metadata, assessment data, or trust score for org B's vendor is returned in the response body.

title: Socket.IO join-project-room rejects a project belonging to a different organization than the connected socket
description: vibrantix-backend/src/core/socket.js (PLAC-012 hotfix, ~line 133-154) verifies `project.organizationId?.toString() !== socket.orgId?.toString()` before allowing a socket to join a `project:{projectId}` room, emitting 'project-room-join-denied' on mismatch. socket.orgId is derived only from the verified JWT during the Socket.IO auth middleware — the client-supplied organizationId is never trusted. Regression guard for this specific check.
preconditions: Org A user with a valid JWT-authenticated Socket.IO connection
A project belonging to org B
steps: Establish a Socket.IO connection authenticated as an org A user
Emit 'join-project-room' with { projectId: <org B's project ID> }
Observe the emitted response event
expectedResult: Socket receives 'project-room-join-denied' for the org B project; the socket is never added to that project's room and receives no subsequent scan-progress or workflow events for it.

title: Socket.IO join-project-room rejects a same-org user who is not a member of the target project (project-level isolation within one tenant)
description: Beyond the org-match check (TISO-SEC-005), socket.js calls computeProjectAccessForUser(socket.userId, socket.orgId) and denies the join unless access.isProjectAdmin or access.projectIds includes the requested projectId — enforcing project-level isolation within the same organization, not just org-level isolation.
preconditions: Org A has Project X and Project Y
User U is a member of Project X only (not project.admin, not assigned to Project Y)
steps: Authenticate User U's Socket.IO connection
Emit 'join-project-room' with { projectId: <Project Y's ID> }
expectedResult: Socket receives 'project-room-join-denied' — same-org membership alone is insufficient; User U never joins Project Y's room and receives no Project Y events.

title: PolicyRepository.search() must not silently drop the organizationId filter when orgId resolves to null/undefined
description: policy.repository.js:358-368 builds the $text search filter and only adds organizationId with `if (orgId !== null && orgId !== undefined) filter.organizationId = orgId;` — if the caller ever passes a null/undefined orgId (e.g. an upstream bug fails to resolve req.orgId, or a future public/global search route reuses this method without threading orgId through), the $text query silently runs across ALL organizations' policies with no org filter at all. This method has no active route calling it today (verified via repo-wide search), but the latent contract is unsafe by construction and must be fixed defensively before any endpoint is wired to it.
preconditions: Direct access to PolicyRepository.search() in a test harness with a seeded multi-tenant Policy collection
steps: Seed policies for org A and org B with an overlapping search term
Call PolicyRepository.search(null, { q: '<shared term>' }) directly
Call PolicyRepository.search(undefined, { q: '<shared term>' }) directly
expectedResult: Current behavior: both calls return matching policies from BOTH org A and org B (no organizationId clause is added to the Mongo filter) — this is a defect. Expected/fixed behavior: the method should throw or return an empty result set when orgId is null/undefined, never silently search cross-tenant.

title: assistant-service RAG bridge call includes organizationId and the Python retrieval backend must filter embeddings by it
description: assistant-service/src/services/RAGBridgeService.ts threads organizationId through to the Python backend payload (organization_id field, ~line 196) on every retrieval call. This verifies end-to-end that a query from org A's assistant session never returns document chunks indexed for org B, i.e. the org_id metadata filter is actually enforced on the vector store side, not just passed and ignored.
preconditions: Org A has an indexed evidence/policy document containing a distinctive, unique phrase
Org B has no such document
Valid JWT for a user in org B
steps: As an org B user, ask the AI Assistant a question whose answer would only be found in org A's uniquely-phrased document
Inspect the RAG context chunks returned to the LLM and the final answer/citations
expectedResult: No org A document chunks appear in the retrieval context or citations for org B's session; the assistant responds that it has no relevant information rather than surfacing org A's content.

title: Project detail endpoint rejects a projectId belonging to another organization even when the caller is authenticated to a valid org
description: project.model.js stores organizationId as a required, indexed field. Any endpoint resolving a project by :id (e.g. GET /api/projects/:id, or GET /api/risks?projectId=) must verify project.organizationId matches req.orgId before returning data or accepting the projectId as a valid scope filter.
preconditions: Two orgs (A, B), each with an active project
Valid JWT for a user in org A
steps: As an org A user, call GET /api/projects/:id using org B's project ID
As an org A user, call a project-scoped list endpoint (e.g. risks, evidence) passing org B's projectId as a query parameter
expectedResult: Both requests are rejected with 403/404, or (for the list endpoint) return an empty result set — org B's project name, code, milestones, budget, or associated records are never returned to an org A caller.

title: Cached API responses (analytics, dashboard, posture summaries) are keyed with orgId as part of the cache key, not just resource type
description: Cross-cutting audit: any Redis cache key construction of the form `${resource}:${id}` without an orgId component risks Org A receiving Org B's cached payload if identifiers ever collide, and prevents clean per-tenant cache invalidation on offboarding. Verify concretely for the cloud-posture and risk analytics caches which are the most cache-heavy paths (risk-management-service posture snapshots, cloud-posture-runtime.js).
preconditions: Two orgs (A, B) with a project whose ObjectId-derived cache key component could theoretically collide, or with matching resource-type cache keys
steps: Trigger a cached analytics/posture read for org A (populates cache)
Trigger the same analytics/posture read for org B immediately after
Inspect the actual Redis key names used (via redis-cli KEYS or MONITOR in a test environment) and the returned payload for org B
expectedResult: Redis keys include orgId as a namespace segment (e.g. `${orgId}:posture:${projectId}`), and org B's response reflects only org B's data — never a cached org A payload.

title: Evidence file confirm endpoint pattern (s3Key org-prefix check) is applied consistently to every service that accepts a presigned-upload confirm, not just evidence-management
description: Regression/consistency guard extending EVID-SEC-003's s3Key-prefix pattern (evidence-upload.controller.js checks s3Key.startsWith('evidence/{req.orgId}/')) — verify the same class of check exists for any other module with direct-to-S3 presigned uploads scoped by tenant (e.g. trust-vault-service certification uploads, vendor-service vendor evidence uploads).
preconditions: Valid JWT for a user in org A
A presigned upload URL generated for org A's own s3Key prefix in trust-vault-service or vendor-service
steps: As an org A user, call the presigned-upload confirm endpoint in trust-vault-service (or vendor-service vendor-evidence route) with a forged s3Key beginning with another org's prefix
expectedResult: Request is rejected with 403 — the confirm endpoint validates the s3Key prefix against req.orgId before persisting any file record, mirroring the evidence-management protection.
